solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not au fait with recent developments in play, presumably

definitions.text: Not au fait with recent developments
definitions.meaning: someone behind the times, no longer informed about what is going on
in rugby or football a ball in touch is dead, so a ball not in touch is still live on the field

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: lacking current knowledge, and (of a ball) not having crossed the touchline, so still live.

clue.text: See 10
Initiate without constituent of protein

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner or novice, someone newly initiated
sine is Latin for without, as in sine die

explanation.surface: A newcomer is being inducted without some part of a protein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initiate' looks like a verb but is a noun here, a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrosine is one of the amino acids that build proteins, so it is a protein constituent.

clue.text: Area over pub half-full with Tim O'Connor performing

indicators.note: half of the word full means only its first two letters are kept
Tim O'Connor performing suggests his name is put through its paces, rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: An actor named Tim O'Connor is on stage upstairs at a pub that is half full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-full' gives just FU; Tim O'Connor is an invented performer whose name, once 'performing' shuffles it, ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs often have a hireable room upstairs for private parties and meetings.

clue.text: Workers here in ravages of North Pole show details

indicators.note: ravages means wrecks or devastates, so the letters that follow are smashed into a new order
read as de-tails: show loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A programme describes how the North Pole is being ravaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'details' cuts the W from 'show', giving SHO; that joins OF and NORTHPOLE as anagram fodder for 'ravages'. 'Of' looks like a link word but is part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The shop floor is the production area of a factory, where the manual staff work.

clue.text: Wild dreams actors are not suffering as much after last of closures delayed

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a production

indicators.note: delayed means one letter turns up later in the phrase than it should

parts.note: less in pain means hurting to a smaller degree

indicators.note: last of closures picks the final letter of that word

explanation.surface: Performers say they hurt less now that the closures have been postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delayed' pushes one S of LESSINPAIN further along, giving LESINSPAIN; 'last of closures' says that the letter is an S.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles in Spain are daydreams or fanciful hopes, much like castles in the air.

clue.text: See 23
Winding most of reel up is, in 24 hours, very minor encouragement

indicators.note: winding a reel up turns its letters back to front in a down clue
up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a spool is a reel for thread or film

indicators.note: is goes inside, contained by the word for a day

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours, so the phrase is read as a day
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rewinding nearly all of a reel over a day gets only feeble cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding ... up' reverses the trimmed reel (SPOO, after 'most of' drops its L). '24 hours' is A DAY, with 'in' setting IS inside it. The definition is what one says to a toddler who stumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is said to comfort a small child who has stumbled, a mild bit of reassurance.

clue.text: After Putin's agreement, pound sterling critical on this

parts.note: da is Russian for yes, the agreement of a Russian such as Putin

indicators.note: pound means to batter or beat, so the letters of the word sterling are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Once Putin agrees, the pound sterling is in a critical state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like part of the currency but is the anagram signal for 'sterling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals put patients in a critical condition on a register of the gravely ill.

clue.text: Anthropomorphic trial gets disrupted by Italian city tenor

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of gets are scrambled

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A trial of human likeness is upset by a tenor from an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Turing proposed this test of whether a machine's conversation can pass for human; 'disrupted' shuffles the four letters of 'gets'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing's test asks whether a machine can pass for a human in conversation, judging human-like behaviour.

clue.text: Embarking on university route musical widow's bound to be truthful

indicators.note: embarking on means starting off, so this piece is placed at the front
bound means encircled or tied around, so the route wraps the widow

parts.note: a path is a way or route
Yoko Ono is the widow of the musician John Lennon

explanation.surface: Joining a university route, the widow of a musician is obliged to be honest.
explanation.walkthrough: Yoko Ono is the widow of the musician John Lennon. 'Embarking on' places U first, and 'bound' wraps the route around the widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given under a sworn vow is legally required to be honest.

clue.text: 1 in 100 in the bag, on the rack or on board

definitions.text: 1 in 100 in the bag, on the rack or on board

parts.words: 1 in 100 in the bag, on the rack or on board
parts.note: a word game set has a hundred lettered pieces, drawn from a bag, kept on a player's rack and then laid on the board

explanation.surface: One of a hundred items moves from bag to rack to board.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' looks like a cross-reference to 1 across but is just one; 'rack' and 'board' suggest a ship or torture before the word game.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard English set of the board game contains exactly a hundred lettered pieces.

clue.text: Difficult children covered by termly contract for race

parts.note: steep means hard to climb or excessive, hence difficult

indicators.note: covered by means the children sit inside the contract

parts.note: a lease is a contract for a fixed term

explanation.surface: Unruly youngsters are included in a school contract for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A lease runs for a fixed term, hence 'termly contract'; 'covered by' puts the children inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race over fences and ditches, or a track event with hurdles and water jumps.

clue.text: Some interminable traffic block heading north broken by endless line of police stewards

indicators.note: broken by means the reversed run is split open with the police line inside
heading north in a down clue means reading from bottom to top
interminable means without an end, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a jam is a block in the flow of traffic

indicators.note: endless means the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: a cordon is a line of police holding back a crowd

explanation.surface: Part of an endless traffic jam heading north is breached by a police line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' and 'endless' trim the ends; 'heading north' turns the trimmed word and the jam upwards, as this is a down clue; 'broken by' splits them with the trimmed police line.
explanation.definitionFit: A major-domo is the chief steward running a grand household.

clue.text: Baffled, one changed sides (XI on it)

indicators.note: baffled means confused or perplexed, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: One baffled player swapped teams, with a cricket eleven on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baffled' rearranges ONECHANGED. XI is the Roman numeral eleven, so the definition says a figure with eleven sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygon with eleven sides and eleven angles, from Greek hendeka (eleven).

clue.text: A nasty piece of work's casing what beer joints?

indicators.note: casing means enclosing, so the nasty piece of work wraps around the query

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person; louse's here gives the letters with the S
eh is a query meaning what?

explanation.surface: A villain's surroundings make us ask what beer has to do with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what' as a question is the interjection EH; 'casing' puts it inside the plural of the nasty piece of work, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns and pubs, places where ale is served.

clue.text: See 4
Is it demanding 1 Burj Khalifa, 2 Tokyo Sky Tree, 3 Abraj Al Bait?

definitions.text: Is it demanding 1 Burj Khalifa, 2 Tokyo Sky Tree, 3 Abraj Al Bait?

parts.words: Is it demanding 1 Burj Khalifa, 2 Tokyo Sky Tree, 3 Abraj Al Bait?
parts.note: the list ranks the world's highest structures, a ranking of lofty buildings that is also a difficult demand

explanation.surface: Is this ranked list of the world's tallest buildings a tough request?
explanation.walkthrough: The three buildings are the world's tallest tower, tallest broadcasting tower and a giant Mecca clock tower, listed in height ranking.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult request is idiomatically lofty, and the list is literally a ranking of lofty things.

clue.text: See 17
Public transport needed, writer boards 09

indicators.note: boards means gets on, so the writer is placed inside

parts.note: zero gives O and nine gives the nine Muses of Greek myth
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: Buses are needed, and a writer gets on at 09.
explanation.walkthrough: '09' is O (zero) and MUSES (the nine Muses); 'boards' puts NIB inside after the M. 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal word for buses, vehicles carrying the general public.

clue.text: Wet man who prescribes lace support

parts.note: to lace a drink is to spike or doctor it
to foster is to nurture or support

explanation.surface: A soaked physician suggests a lace brace.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme this physician went to Gloucester in a shower of rain, so he is the wet man.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme figure is a physician who gets soaked by stepping in a puddle.

clue.text: See 5
See 24
You finally moved out of Apartment 4D, The Mill, East Bergholt, Suffolk

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: moved out of means a letter leaves the following word

parts.note: 4D spelt out is four and D

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of that word

explanation.surface: A tenant moves out of an apartment at a mill in a Suffolk village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You finally' is U; 'moved out of' removes it from FOURD, leaving FORD. The Mill is the one John Constable painted.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatford is the hamlet in East Bergholt parish whose mill appears in Constable's paintings.

clue.text: It's futile — silent audience finally strangles lousy gags

indicators.note: strangles means grips around the throat, so the gags are held inside

parts.note: mum means saying nothing, silent

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of that word
lousy means bad, so the letters of gags are badly ordered

explanation.surface: A hushed crowd chokes on poor jokes, which seems pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lousy' shuffles 'gags' to GSGA, and 'strangles' grips it inside MUM plus the E from 'audience finally'. A mug is a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointless activity that only a fool would undertake is idiomatically a dupe's pursuit.

clue.text: In a reversal of fortune, investment is ultimately the worst of the lot

definitions.text: ultimately the worst of the lot

indicators.note: in means the investment sits within the turned word
a reversal of means the following word is read backwards

parts.note: lot means fate or fortune
capital is money invested

explanation.surface: In a financial reverse, the investment proves the worst of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a reversal of' turns 'fortune' backwards into TOL, and 'In' slots the investment between its O and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom said when a final misfortune crowns a series of bad ones.

clue.text: See 2
Fruit extract for many geezers to regularly offload

indicators.note: regularly offload means drop letters at even intervals, here every third one

explanation.surface: Lots of chaps have to keep getting rid of citrus peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly offload' deletes every third letter of FORMANYGEEZERSTO (F, M, Y, E, R, O). 'for' looks like a link word but is part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Grated citrus peel used to flavour food is an extract of the fruit.
